subject: URGENT: Third-party peering disruption impacting EU & APAC — immediate routing options and customer steps
body_summary: Cloud provider peering outage caused degraded connectivity for EU and APAC PoPs. Immediate mitigation: opt customers into cross-region reroute or set region preference headers. Internal action items include publishing customer notice, enabling emergency reroute via Console, collecting telemetry, and scheduling an internal RCA.
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: ops@brightretail.com, sarah.taylor@acme-ecom.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Third-party peering disruption impacting EU & APAC — immediate routing options and customer steps

Hi —

We’re seeing a network peering disruption at one of our upstream providers that is causing increased 5xx errors and higher tail latency for requests routed through EU (eu-west-1) and APAC (apac-south-1) edge PoPs. Impact window started ~08:40 UTC and is intermittent; some customers are seeing elevated error rates on generation and embeddings endpoints.

What we’re doing now (short):
- Our traffic routing layer is detecting degraded egress for affected regions and will attempt automatic fallbacks where configured.
- We’ve opened ticket INC-20260504-78 with the provider (network-ops@cloudpeer.io) and are in active coordination.

Immediate actions for customers (two options):
1) Soft opt-in (recommended, fastest): Enable account-level Emergency Reroute in Console -> Traffic Control. This routes new requests to a selectable fallback region (we recommend us-east-1 for most EU/APAC customers until peering is restored).
   - Console path: https://console.redwood.ai/traffic-control/reroute
2) Application-level override: Add header X-Redwood-Region-Preference: us-east-1 to requests or set region param in SDKs. Example (curl):
   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>"
     -H "X-Redwood-Region-Preference: us-east-1"
     -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"Hi"}'

Rollback: remove header or disable Emergency Reroute once provider confirms resolution.

We’ve attached a short diagnostic snippet showing elevated peer latency and SYN drops for affected PoPs. If you want us to enable Emergency Reroute on your behalf, reply with: "Please opt my account into Emergency Reroute to us-east-1 (BrightRetail account id: BR-9876)" and we’ll enable it immediately and follow up with telemetry.

Apologies for the interruption — we’ll post updates to INC-20260504-78 and the Console banner.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Eng, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: diag-snippet-20260504.txt (text/plain)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: URGENT: Third-party peering disruption impacting EU & APAC — immediate routing options and customer steps

On Mon, May 4, 2026 at 09:12 AM Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com> wrote:
> We’re seeing a network peering disruption at one of our upstream providers ...

Thanks, Jasmine — good summary. Quick operational steps I’ve executed and recommend we standardize in the incident runbook: 

1) Console emergency reroute API (admin) — use for customers who ask us to opt them in: 
   curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/accounts/BR-9876/traffic_reroute"
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>"
     -H "Content-Type: application/json"
     -d '{"mode":"regional_prefer","preferred_regions":["us-east-1"],"reason":"upstream_peering_disruption_20260504"}'

2) Verify health checks and KV cache warming after reroute: 
   - Validate sample generation for the customer’s typical payload sizes (we are seeing worst latency at ~1k tokens).
   - Run embedding smoke test against their vectors endpoint.

3) Monitoring and rollback criteria: 
   - If 5xx rate drops below 0.5% for 15m and provider confirms route restoration, start staged rollback to original region.

4) Messaging: I’ll draft a one-paragraph customer notice to send from support. Vanessa, can you send the notice and note who opted in?

Also tagging Markus for a quick sanity check on cross-region cost and cache-warm implications.

— Laura
Director, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

- Status: Provider reports partial mitigation at 13:45 UTC; our telemetry shows error rates trending down but still noisy in apac-south-1.
- Actions taken: Emergency Reroute enabled for BR-9876 and AC-5321 to us-east-1 (Vanessa). We captured request/response traces for 10:30–11:15 UTC and attached a short diagnostic snippet.
- Next steps (internal):

   * Update incident runbook: add explicit Console API curl snippet and rollback criteria (Laura).
   * Build an automated opt-in flow (SRE/Product) so support can enable reroutes without manual token usage (Markus).
   * Customer follow-up: Vanessa to send a closing note with traces and link to INC-20260504-78-EXT for SLA requests.

We’ll close out this thread after the RCA and customer follow-ups are complete.
